Use Jupyter notebooks with the project's R

Source: R/use_pixi_jupyter.R
use_pixi_jupyter.Rd

Experimental. This may change, see https://github.com/roaldarbol/rpix/issues/184.

Set the project up for Jupyter notebooks, so they run with the R of the project's environments:

  • It adds a jupyter environment with JupyterLab, of its own, so the environments with R don't get Python and JupyterLab.

  • It adds IRkernel (r-irkernel) to each environment with R, and, where an environment has Python, ipykernel.

  • It writes a kernel for each of those environments into the project, in .jupyter/kernels/, named e.g. "R (Pixi: default)" or "R (Pixi: r44)". A kernel starts its environment's R with pixi run --environment, so Pixi activates the environment, also on Windows. The kernels have no paths of this computer in them, so commit them with the project.

  • It adds a jupyter task that starts JupyterLab with those kernels: pixi_run("jupyter"), or pixi run jupyter in a terminal.

rpix doesn't use the ir kernel that conda-forge's IRkernel brings, as a kernel of that name in your own Jupyter folder, e.g. from IRkernel::installspec(), would be used instead.

Run it again after adding an environment, to add that environment's kernel.

Usage

use_pixi_jupyter(path = NULL)

Arguments

path

The project. Defaults to the project of the running Pixi environment, or the working directory.

Value

The path to the project's manifest, invisibly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Needs Pixi, and adds JupyterLab and IRkernel to the project
use_pixi_jupyter()
pixi_run("jupyter")
} # }
